name: Seal Brown
lede: Seal Brown carries over from Ridgway's 1886 Nomenclature of Colors, and ColorHub's warm screen swatch sits about 18 color-distance units from Ridgway's own cooler, grayer plate.

sections.title: A swatch warmer than the plate
sections.body:
Ridgway's plates give Seal Brown at hue 5‴, tone m, on plate XXXIX, and the name carries over from his earlier 1886 *Nomenclature of Colors* [1]. The Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 census files it, in block 81, as a deep brown, Munsell 4.2YR 2.2/6.0 [1].

ColorHub's screen swatch, #59260B, is a warm, saturated red-brown, but Ridgway's own plate reads as a cooler, grayer #574C46, about 18 color-distance units apart[1]. The closest other library name is [[dusty-mahogany]], just under 5.7 units off, with [[mahogany]] a touch further at 6.3 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Seal Brown in 1,561 of 23,781 paintings, 6.6 percent, more often as a mid-tone or shadow than a highlight [2]. It peaks in the 1540s, in 23 of 163 paintings, more than double its average rate, and favors court portraitists: Jean Baptiste Vanmour carries it in 16 of 29 dated works [2]. Spanish and Italian paintings carry it a little above the archive's base rate [2]. It shares canvases with [[maroon]], [[oxblood]], and [[mahogany]] far more than chance alone predicts [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
